intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently for an authentic culinary adventure.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Street Food
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, famous for its colorful lanterns, tailor shops, and incredible street food scene. Try White Rose Dumplings, Cao Lau noodles, and Banh Mi Phuong — considered one of the best Banh Mi in Vietnam. On the 14th of each lunar month, the town turns off electric lights and floats lanterns on the river.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic mountain roads. The route offers breathtaking views of the ocean, jungle, and coastline between Da Nang and Hue — a quintessential backpacker experience immortalized by Top Gear.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat Tour & Local Market Visit
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, navigating narrow canals by wooden boat, visiting floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and rice paper factories. Sample tropical fruits and freshly cooked local dishes while experiencing the rural Vietnamese way of life.
experiences.location: Cai Rang Floating Market, Can Tho, Mekong Delta

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's legendary backpacker district on Bui Vien Street. Enjoy incredibly cheap street food including Banh Trang Tron (rice paper salad), grilled skewers, and fresh spring rolls while soaking up the vibrant nightlife, live music, and the electric energy of fellow backpackers from around the world.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Backpacker District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage. Take a budget airport taxi or grab app ride to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a quick late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour street stall or convenience store if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food
meals.dinner: Late night street food near the hotel or convenience store snack (budget ~50,000 VND / $2 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Download the Grab app before landing for affordable rides. Exchange some cash at the airport for initial expenses. Keep arrival light — rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, explore the immediate beachfront area on foot. Take a slow morning walk along the beach, get oriented with the neighborhood, and locate nearby street food stalls and local markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local market to experience Vietnamese daily life and culture. Browse fresh produce, local snacks, and handmade goods. Pick up cheap souvenirs or street food ingredients. Spend time people-watching and soaking in the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the local night market or food street near the resort. Try multiple street food dishes from different vendors — a true Vietnamese backpacker experience. Sample local favorites like bánh mì, gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), and chè (sweet dessert soup).

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a street cart (~20,000–30,000 VND / ~$1.20 USD)
meals.lunch: Local market food stall — cơm tấm (broken rice with pork) (~40,000 VND / ~$1.60 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market street food crawl — try 3–4 small dishes (~100,000 VND / ~$4 USD total)

day_by_day.notes: April in Vietnam can be hot and humid. Stay hydrated with coconut water from street vendors (~20,000 VND). Use this day to recover from jet lag and get your bearings.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a nearby Buddhist pagoda or temple for a cultural experience. Observe morning prayers and incense rituals. Many pagodas are free to enter — dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees). Take time to appreciate the architecture and peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (100,000–150,000 VND/day) to explore the surrounding countryside or coastal roads. Visit a nearby fishing village to see traditional boats and interact with local fishermen. Take photos of colorful fishing vessels and daily village life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local seafood street market for dinner. In coastal Vietnam, fresh seafood is affordable and delicious. Try grilled squid, clams, and shrimp cooked at open-air stalls. Join locals sitting on plastic stools at low tables.

meals.breakfast: Phở from a local street stall (~40,000 VND / ~$1.60 USD)
meals.lunch: Bánh xèo (Vietnamese sizzling crepe) from a roadside vendor (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood at a local street seafood market (~120,000–150,000 VND / ~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Motorbike rental requires an international license or local permit in some areas. Bicycles are a safer and cheaper alternative for short distances. Always negotiate rental prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget local bus or shared minivan to the nearest major cultural town or city. Explore the old quarter or historic district on foot. Visit a free or low-cost museum to learn about Vietnamese history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local craft villages or artisan workshops in the area. Watch locals make traditional goods like lanterns, ceramics, or lacquerware. Many workshops are free to visit and offer affordable handmade items for purchase.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free cultural performance if available (check local listings for traditional music or dance shows at cultural centers). Return to the hotel area and enjoy dinner at a local com binh dan (budget rice restaurant).

meals.breakfast: Xôi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street cart (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cơm bình dân (budget set meal with rice, meat, and vegetables) (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Local buses are extremely cheap (10,000–20,000 VND per trip). Ask hotel staff for the nearest bus stop and routes. Carry a small backpack with water and snacks for day trips.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or low-cost walking tour of the local area (many hostels and guesthouses offer these). Learn about the history, architecture, and street food culture from a local guide. Visit a traditional Vietnamese house or communal hall if accessible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a local beach or riverside area. Relax, swim, or simply enjoy the scenery. Rent a cheap beach chair (~30,000–50,000 VND) or lay on a sarong. Explore tide pools or take a short hike along coastal paths.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a meal with locals by joining a budget cooking class (many run for 150,000–300,000 VND). Learn to make 2–3 classic Vietnamese dishes. Alternatively, join other backpackers at a local hostel common area for cheap beers and social connection.

meals.breakfast: Bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) at a local eatery (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Mì Quảng (turmeric noodles) from a street vendor (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cooking class meal included OR local restaurant dinner (~80,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Check TripAdvisor or hostel notice boards for free walking tours. Budget cooking classes are a great way to meet fellow travelers and learn authentic recipes to recreate at home.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby natural attraction — a waterfall, national park, or scenic viewpoint. Hire a local xe ôm (motorbike taxi) or join a budget group tour for the ride. Bring water, sunscreen, and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the natural site. Hike local trails, swim in natural pools if available, or simply enjoy the scenery and take photos. Interact with minority ethnic communities if in a highland area — always respectful and culturally sensitive.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Reward yourself with a street food feast. Explore a different area of the local food scene — look for a busy food alley or street with multiple vendors.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (rice porridge/congee) from a morning street stall (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or food from a roadside stall near the natural attraction (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food alley dinner — try chả giò (fried spring rolls), nem lụi, and fresh fruit (~100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Entrance fees to national parks and nature reserves are typically 20,000–50,000 VND for Vietnamese sites. Bring insect repellent for jungle or forest areas. Stay on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local wet market at dawn (5:00–7:00 AM) for an authentic cultural experience. Watch vendors set up, observe the chaotic energy, and taste fresh tropical fruits. This is one of the most genuine glimpses into Vietnamese daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local neighborhood away from tourist areas. Walk through residential streets, visit a local café for Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá), and observe everyday life. Find a local park where elderly residents do morning tai chi or play chess.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from a scenic spot — beach, hilltop, or rooftop café. Enjoy a bia hơi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) at a street-side beer stall with locals. This is a quintessential Vietnamese backpacker experience.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and bánh tiêu (hollow fried doughnuts) from the wet market (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Hủ tiếu (clear noodle soup) at a local neighborhood restaurant (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bia hơi street stall with grilled snacks and appetizers (~80,000–100,000 VND including beers)

day_by_day.notes: Bia hơi culture is a must-experience in Vietnam. Sit on tiny plastic stools, order fresh beer, and share snacks with strangers. It's social, cheap, and deeply Vietnamese.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a cultural heritage site — a UNESCO-listed area, ancient citadel, or historic complex nearby. Many are affordable or free. Take time to read information boards and understand the historical significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art gallery, cultural center, or handicraft cooperative. Many are free to enter. Look for locally made items to purchase as affordable, authentic souvenirs — avoid mass-produced tourist trinkets.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer local restaurant for dinner (still budget-friendly by Western standards). Try a full Vietnamese set meal with multiple courses — soup, main dish, rice, and dessert. Celebrate the near-end of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì ốp la (bánh mì with fried egg) (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls) and bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodles) (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant with full Vietnamese set meal (~150,000–200,000 VND — a budget splurge!)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting heritage sites, dress modestly and follow all posted rules. Photography may be restricted in certain sacred areas. Hiring a local guide for heritage sites adds context and supports the local economy (~100,000–150,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Last full day exploration — revisit your favorite spots from the trip. Take final photos, buy last-minute souvenirs from local markets (not airport shops — prices are much higher there). Pack items carefully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the beach or a local café. Reflect on the trip, write in a travel journal, or chat with fellow travelers. Try any street foods you haven't yet sampled. Consider a cheap Vietnamese massage (~100,000–150,000 VND/hour) as a relaxing treat.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Vietnam — go back to your favorite street food spot or try something new. Toast the trip with a local drink: sinh tố (fresh fruit smoothie), soda chanh (lime soda), or a final bia hơi.

meals.breakfast: Dim sum or bánh bao (steamed buns) from a morning cart (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Your favorite dish from the trip — revisit the best vendor you found
meals.dinner: Final street food feast — order everything you loved over the past 10 days (~120,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — dried foods, coffee, and spices are great budget gifts. Vacuum-sealed bags help with liquids. Check airline baggage restrictions before buying bulky items.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early, complete final packing, and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a quick street breakfast near the hotel. Head to the airport with plenty of time — aim to arrive at least 2–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Vietnamese coffee or snacks. Reflect on an incredible 10-day budget adventure through Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Vietnam with unforgettable memories, a full stomach, and a very happy wallet.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese street breakfast — phở or bánh mì (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or convenience store (budget ~100,000–150,000 VND at airport prices)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Keep some VND for airport transport and last meals. Leftover VND can be exchanged back at the airport (keep exchange receipts). Leave a review for your accommodation and favorite street food spots to help future budget travelers.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and do a brief orientation of the resort facilities. Get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a quick late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour convenience store or hotel room service (~100,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival is late at night. Confirm resort transfer in advance. Exchange some cash to Vietnamese Dong (VND) at the airport for convenience. April in Vietnam can be warm and humid; stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. After eating, take a morning stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Explore the immediate coastal area around Aegean Bliss Resort, take in the ocean views, and settle into the local rhythm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local market or town center to get a feel for Vietnamese daily life. Browse fresh produce stalls, local handicrafts, and interact with vendors. Pick up a few snacks and essentials. If near a cultural site, visit a local pagoda or community temple for a first taste of Vietnamese culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby beachside strip or local restaurant area for your first proper Vietnamese dinner. Explore the evening atmosphere, try local street food vendors, and enjoy the warm coastal night air.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a simple Vietnamese breakfast of Bánh Mì and iced coffee at a local café (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or Bún bò Huế at a local mid-range restaurant (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Grilled seafood and fresh spring rolls at a beachside local eatery (~150,000–250,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: This is your orientation day — don't over-schedule. Download Google Maps offline and get a local SIM card at a nearby phone shop for easy navigation. April is generally sunny along coastal Vietnam.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise beach walk or light jog along the shoreline. Afterward, visit a nearby fishing village to witness local fishermen returning with their morning catch. This is a great cultural and photographic experience unique to coastal Vietnam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a half-day cultural excursion to a nearby historical site, ancient temple complex, or traditional craft village. Hire a local guide or join a small group tour (~200,000–350,000 VND) for deeper context. Explore at a relaxed pace, taking photos and engaging with artisans or locals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and explore a local night market or street food alley. Sample Vietnamese street food classics and soak in the vibrant evening atmosphere with locals and fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (Vietnamese rice porridge) or Xôi (sticky rice) from a street vendor (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Phở or Bún thịt nướng at a local pho shop (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food feast at the night market — try Bánh Xèo (sizzling crepes), Nem cuốn (fresh rolls), and local grilled skewers (~100,000–180,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Carry a small daypack with water and sunscreen. Bargaining at markets is expected — be polite and enjoy the process.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning cooking class or street food tour offered by local operators near the resort area. Learn to prepare 2–3 classic Vietnamese dishes such as Gỏi cuốn, Phở, or Cơm tấm. This is an immersive cultural and culinary experience (~300,000–500,000 VND per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the class, visit a nearby museum, cultural center, or heritage site to deepen your understanding of the region's history. Alternatively, rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and explore surrounding villages and rice paddies at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset from the beach or a rooftop bar. Treat yourself to a mid-range seafood dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant to celebrate your first full days in Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Included in cooking class or grab Bánh Mì from a street cart (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class, or a light meal at a local com binh dan (everyday Vietnamese rice shop) (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Grilled prawns, clams in lemongrass, and steamed fish at a mid-range seafood restaurant (~200,000–350,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance, especially during peak season. Ask the instructor about regional specialties unique to this part of Vietnam.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby natural attraction — this could be a national park, waterfall, cave system, or scenic viewpoint depending on the resort's location. Start early to beat the heat and crowds. Hire a motorbike taxi (xe ôm) or join a day tour (~300,000–600,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the natural site or hike a nearby trail with scenic views. Pack a light lunch or stop at a local roadside eatery along the way. Take in Vietnam's stunning natural landscape and biodiversity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Rest and refresh, then head out for a casual evening exploring local cafés and dessert shops. Try Chè (Vietnamese sweet soup dessert) or Kem (Vietnamese ice cream).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a quick street-side Bánh Mì (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside local food near the natural attraction (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a local Vietnamese restaurant — try Cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) (~80,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for hiking. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and at least 1.5L of water per person. Check weather conditions before heading out as April can bring afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a nearby town or city by local bus or rented scooter. Visit a bustling wet market in the morning when it's most lively. Observe the incredible variety of fresh produce, spices, meats, and seafood that form the backbone of Vietnamese cuisine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cultural or religious landmark — a well-known pagoda, Confucian temple, or French colonial-era building. Spend time wandering the old quarter or historic district, photographing architecture and street scenes. Pop into local boutique shops for handmade souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour in the town center (~200,000–350,000 VND) or self-guide your own food crawl through popular local eateries and street stalls. This is a great evening for sampling widely.

meals.breakfast: Hủ Tiếu (clear noodle soup) or Mì Quảng (turmeric noodles) at a local breakfast spot (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bánh Căn or Bánh Bèo (regional savory rice cakes) at a traditional local eatery (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl — sample 4–5 different dishes from various vendors (~150,000–250,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Rent a quality scooter from a reputable shop and wear a helmet at all times. Keep a copy of your passport and travel insurance details handy. Bargain respectfully at souvenir shops.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip or kayaking excursion on nearby waters — a river delta, lagoon, bay, or island depending on the resort location. This is a quintessential Vietnamese experience offering beautiful scenery and a different perspective on the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit floating villages, mangrove forests, or small islands accessible by boat. Interact with local fishermen and learn about their way of life. Snorkel or swim in clear coastal waters if available.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxing evening. Treat yourself to a traditional Vietnamese massage (~200,000–350,000 VND for 60–90 minutes) at a local spa to soothe tired muscles from a week of exploring.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort (~included or ~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on a boat or at a floating restaurant (~150,000–250,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a resort-adjacent restaurant or upscale local eatery — try Lẩu (Vietnamese hot pot) for a fun communal meal (~200,000–350,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat tour in advance. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. Apply waterproof sunscreen and bring a hat and sunglasses. The week's halfway point — a great time to review plans for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site or major cultural attraction if within day-trip distance (e.g., Hội An Ancient Town, Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, or Huế Imperial Citadel depending on your location). Arrive early to explore before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage site — wander through ancient streets, visit assembly halls, historic houses, or ruins. Join a guided walking tour (~150,000–250,000 VND) for historical context. Browse artisan workshops and pick up authentic local crafts as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: If in Hội An, enjoy the famous lantern-lit old town in the evening — it's magical after dark. Release a lantern on the river (~20,000–30,000 VND) and dine at one of the town's celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Cao Lầu (Hội An specialty noodles) or Cơm Gà (chicken rice) at a traditional breakfast spot (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.lunch: White Rose dumplings and Bánh Mì Phượng (if in Hội An) or regional specialty at a local restaurant (~80,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-reviewed heritage town restaurant — try set menus featuring local specialties (~200,000–350,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Hội An Old Town entry ticket (~120,000 VND) if visiting. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets. Respect dress codes when entering temples and pagodas — cover shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a local art gallery, photography exhibition, or cultural workshop (lacquerware, silk weaving, pottery, or lantern making). This is a hands-on way to engage with Vietnamese artistic traditions and bring home a unique skill or handmade souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beachfront area for a relaxing afternoon. Swim, sunbathe, or try a water sport such as paddleboarding or snorkeling. Alternatively, explore any remaining local areas you haven't visited yet — a final sweep of hidden gems and neighborhood streets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of the best local restaurants in the area. Splurge slightly on this meal to celebrate the trip. Share dishes family-style with travel companions or fellow backpackers you've met along the way.

meals.breakfast: Vietnamese-style breakfast spread — Phở, fried eggs, fresh fruit, and Vietnamese drip coffee (cà phê phin) (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café — fresh coconut, fruit smoothies, and a sandwich or rice dish (~80,000–130,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a top-rated local restaurant — fresh seafood platter, Vietnamese spring rolls, and local dessert (~300,000–500,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to buy any remaining souvenirs and gifts. Check baggage weight limits for your return flight. Back up all your photos. Leave a review for your favorite local restaurants and experiences to help other travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — a peaceful moment to reflect on the journey. Pack your bags and do a final check of the room. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and settle any remaining bills. Store luggage with the concierge if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final few hours of local exploration — visit a nearby café for one last Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá), stroll through a local market, or simply relax by the water. Head to the airport with ample time (arrive 2–3 hours before international departure).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Vietnam with incredible memories, a full stomach, and a deep appreciation for this vibrant and beautiful country. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — Bánh Mì with egg and pâté and a strong cà phê sữa đá (~40,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Light meal at a nearby café or airport restaurant (~80,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Double-check passport, boarding pass, and all documents before leaving the resort. Keep some VND for airport snacks and tips. Declare any food items or purchases over customs limits. Consider writing down your top 3 Vietnam memories — this trip deserves to be remembered in detail!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — rest and recovery after long-haul flight UA.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at 22:30. Private airport transfer arranged by the resort. Welcome cocktail and light refreshments at the resort's beachfront lounge. Brief orientation with your personal concierge. Early rest to prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight dining
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and artisan cocktails at the resort's private lounge upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your resort has arranged a private luxury transfer from the airport. Request a late check-in amenity package — most luxury resorts in Vietnam offer complimentary welcome drinks and a fruit basket for late arrivals. Keep the first night light and restful.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront promenade. Explore the nearby local market to get a first taste of Vietnamese culture, fresh produce, and artisan crafts with your personal guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cyclo (pedicab) tour through the old quarter or heritage streets closest to the resort area. Visit a renowned local pagoda or cultural heritage site. Stop at a traditional Vietnamese lacquerware or silk workshop for a hands-on cultural demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private beach terrace. Dinner at a highly acclaimed local fine-dining restaurant specializing in regional Vietnamese cuisine with contemporary plating.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant featuring pho, banh mi, fresh tropical fruits, and Vietnamese egg coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional Vietnamese set lunch at a heritage house restaurant — com tam (broken rice) with grilled pork, fresh spring rolls, and lotus tea
meals.dinner: Fine-dining dinner at a premium Vietnamese restaurant — tasting menu featuring chả cá Lã Vọng (turmeric fish), bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and premium Vietnamese wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: April is generally warm and pleasant across Vietnam. Pack light breathable clothing, sunscreen, and a hat for outdoor activities. Tip your guide generously — it is culturally appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise boat excursion along the coastline or nearby bay. Enjoy a curated breakfast box on the water prepared by the resort's chef. Snorkeling or kayaking stop at a secluded cove accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a signature Vietnamese herbal spa treatment — the resort's full-body scrub using local ingredients like lemongrass, ginger, and sea salt. Followed by a relaxing steam session and poolside lounging.
day_by_day.evening: Private street food walking tour with a culinary expert guide through the nearest vibrant local neighborhood. Sample bánh mì, bún bò Huế, bánh cuốn, and fresh sugarcane juice from authentic street stalls.

meals.breakfast: Chef-prepared gourmet breakfast box on the morning boat — Vietnamese baguette sandwiches, local cheeses, tropical fruit, and Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled seafood skewers, papaya salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Premium street food crawl — curated 8-stop tasting experience through local markets and street stalls with a private guide, concluding with chè (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup)

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa treatment in advance as slots fill quickly at luxury resorts. The street food tour is best experienced after 6:30 PM when stalls are fully operational and the evening ambiance is at its peak.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip departure by luxury vehicle to a UNESCO World Heritage Site nearby (e.g., Hội An Ancient Town or Huế Imperial Citadel depending on resort location). Morning exploration of the ancient town's lantern-lit streets, merchant houses, and Japanese Covered Bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided tour of tailoring workshops — commission a custom Vietnamese áo dài (traditional dress) or bespoke silk garments. Visit the Assembly Hall of the Fujian Chinese Congregation and local ceramic village. Enjoy a private cooking class with a local chef.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise on a traditional wooden boat with candles and lanterns. Return to resort by private luxury transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — Vietnamese congee (cháo), fried dough sticks (quẩy), and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at a critically acclaimed restaurant in the heritage town — cao lầu (Hội An specialty noodles), white rose dumplings, and fresh herb salads
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the sunset river cruise — premium canapés, Vietnamese wine, and a curated charcuterie spread; followed by light supper at resort upon return

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the heritage town exploration. The custom tailoring typically requires 24–48 hours for completion — plan a pickup on a later day. Carry cash in Vietnamese Dong for small market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided mountain or countryside excursion by luxury 4x4 vehicle. Explore terraced rice paddies, ethnic minority villages, and scenic highland viewpoints. Interact with local artisans and learn about traditional weaving or pottery techniques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Picnic lunch in a scenic natural setting arranged by the resort. Afternoon hike to a hidden waterfall or nature reserve with a certified eco-guide. Optional bamboo rafting or zip-lining experience in the jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Private rooftop dinner under the stars at the resort's exclusive sky dining venue with a personalized multi-course Vietnamese tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service — eggs cooked to order, Vietnamese pâté on fresh baguette, tropical fruit platter, and Vietnamese egg coffee (cà phê trứng)
meals.lunch: Gourmet resort-prepared picnic in the countryside — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruits, Vietnamese rice cakes, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Private sky dining experience — 7-course Vietnamese tasting menu with premium wine pairing, featuring dishes like lobster pho, wagyu beef pho cuốn, and durian soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Confirm weather conditions before the mountain excursion as highland areas can experience afternoon showers in April. Bring insect repellent and a light jacket for higher elevations.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter or seaplane transfer to a remote island or Ha Long Bay-style karst seascape (depending on resort location). Begin a luxury overnight junk cruise with a private cabin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through limestone caves and hidden lagoons. Swimming in emerald waters at a secluded beach accessible only by boat. Guided visit to a floating fishing village to meet local fishermen.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the junk's sundeck. Squid fishing experience off the side of the boat under the stars. Gourmet seafood dinner prepared fresh on board.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at resort before departure — phở bò (beef pho), steamed buns, fresh fruit, and Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the junk — grilled prawns, steamed clams with lemongrass, squid salad, and jasmine rice
meals.dinner: Premium on-board seafood feast — whole steamed fish, lobster thermidor Vietnamese-style, crab claws, and fresh oysters with dipping sauces and premium Vietnamese craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Pack an overnight bag with essentials for the junk cruise — the resort concierge can arrange luggage storage. Bring seasickness medication if needed. The junk cruise is one of the most iconic Vietnamese luxury experiences — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise tai chi session on the junk's sundeck led by an onboard wellness instructor. Morning kayaking to a pristine cave or beach. Brunch on board before returning to the mainland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return transfer to resort. Afternoon at leisure — beach time, resort pool, or optional visit to a local art gallery featuring contemporary Vietnamese artists.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural evening at a traditional water puppet theater performance — one of Vietnam's most unique art forms. Post-show dinner at a celebrated restaurant known for northern Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full brunch on the junk — eggs benedict, Vietnamese noodle soup, tropical fruits, pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at resort upon return — Vietnamese rice paper rolls, pho ga (chicken pho), and cold pressed juices
meals.dinner: Post-theater dinner at a premium northern Vietnamese restaurant — bún chả (grilled pork with noodles), nem cuốn (fresh spring rolls), and bánh đúc nóng, paired with local craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book water puppet theater tickets in advance as performances sell out quickly, especially during peak season. The resort concierge can arrange premium front-row seating.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided temple and pagoda circuit — visit the most significant spiritual sites in the region with a knowledgeable cultural historian guide. Learn about Vietnamese Buddhism, Confucianism, and Taoism through immersive storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vietnamese street food masterclass at a premium cooking school — learn to prepare 5 iconic dishes including pho, bánh xèo, gỏi cuốn, and chè ba màu (three-color dessert). Take home a recipe booklet and a curated spice kit.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop bar experience at one of the region's most celebrated sky bars. Signature cocktails with panoramic city or ocean views. Late dinner at a contemporary Vietnamese fusion restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — dim sum selection, Vietnamese steamed rice cakes (bánh bèo), fresh smoothie bowls, and cold brew Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class — enjoy your own creations as part of the class experience, served with lotus flower tea
meals.dinner: Contemporary Vietnamese fusion tasting menu — wagyu beef cuốn, truffle-infused pho broth, mango sticky rice soufflé, and premium sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is an excellent opportunity to bring back authentic Vietnamese culinary skills. Request vegetarian or dietary-specific alternatives when booking. Dress smart-casual for the rooftop bar.

day_by_day.morning: Private vintage motorcycle sidecar tour through the local countryside and coastal roads — a quintessential Vietnam experience. Stop at scenic viewpoints, local coffee plantations, and a traditional village market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit to a premium Vietnamese coffee estate — learn about the coffee-growing process from bean to cup, with a guided tasting of robusta, arabica, and the legendary weasel coffee (cà phê chồn). Purchase premium coffee to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell beach bonfire dinner arranged by the resort — private setup on the beach with lanterns, fire dancers, and a bespoke menu. Personalized farewell ceremony by the resort team.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — bánh mì with premium Vietnamese charcuterie, avocado, and a signature Vietnamese egg coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a countryside family-run restaurant recommended by your guide — cơm bình dân (home-style rice dishes), caramelized fish in clay pot (cá kho tộ), and fresh herbs
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire farewell dinner — whole roasted suckling pig, grilled lobster, Vietnamese herb salads, sticky rice in bamboo, and a bespoke dessert platter with fireworks sparklers

day_by_day.notes: The motorcycle sidecar tour requires advance booking and safety briefing. Helmets are provided. This is one of the most photogenic experiences in Vietnam — bring your camera. The farewell beach dinner should be booked with the resort at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga or meditation session on the beach led by the resort's wellness instructor. Last swim in the ocean or resort pool. Leisurely packing and checkout preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration of the nearest local neighborhood — pick up last-minute souvenirs including lacquerware, silk scarves, Vietnamese coffee, and hand-embroidered goods. Visit a final local landmark or viewpoint for a memorable farewell photo.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport for departure flight. In-lounge dining at the airport's premium lounge if time permits before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full Vietnamese spread including pho, bánh mì, tropical fruits, and a farewell Vietnamese egg coffee crafted tableside by the barista
meals.lunch: Final local lunch at a beloved neighborhood restaurant — bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup), gỏi bưởi (pomelo salad), and Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.dinner: Premium airport lounge dining or in-flight premium cabin meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in procedures. Request a late checkout from the resort (typically until 2:00 PM for luxury guests) to maximize your final morning. Ensure all custom-tailored items from Day 4 are collected before departure. Keep Vietnamese Dong for any last-minute tips and small purchases.
